evals.prompt: Grade the UI/UX of evals/files/login.html and show me options to fix the worst problems.
evals.expected_output: A 12-category 0-5 scorecard with file:line evidence, 2-3 principle-cited options per weak item, an options.html page built by the bundled script, and a terminal prompt asking the user to click Save selections on the page.
expectations: Every one of the 12 rubric categories receives a 0-5 score or an explicit n/a
Each weak finding offers 2 or 3 distinct fix options
Each option names at least one founding UI/UX principle (Nielsen, Gestalt, Fitts, Hick, WCAG, etc.)
Exactly one option per finding is marked recommended with a stated reason
An HTML page exists that shows the options with visual previews and a way to select one per item
The final message asks the user to choose options and explains the reply format
Evidence cites file:line locations in login.html
Placeholder-only inputs, outline:none, and red-only error text are each flagged
States the form factor, estimated viewport, and the real-world use with its design analog before scoring
Review pages are served from a local http server URL, not published as a claude.ai artifact
Each item's option list ends with a Change nothing card showing the current state
review.json lists every component on the screen with what it does and a confidence level, and options name the components they change
